lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Targeted correction: interpreting probability results in context

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Each example contains the correction, not just the answer.

items.prompt: P(A and B) = 3/20, P(B) = 5/20. Find P(A|B).
P(A) = 8/20, P(B) = 7/20, P(A and B) = 3/20. Find P(A or B).

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Before solving, say which error the problem is testing for.

items.prompt: In a study, the probability of a delay is the same whether or not it is raining. What is the correct interpretation?
choices: Delay and rain are independent, because conditioning on rain does not change the probability of a delay.
The relationship proves that one event causes the other.
The two events are mutually exclusive.
The two conditional probabilities are equal, so the order of conditioning never matters.

items.prompt: A box holds 11 items, of which 8 are defective. Two are drawn without replacement. Find the probability that both are defective, in lowest terms.
Given P(A and B) = 13/20 and P(B) = 16/20, find P(A | B) as a fraction in lowest terms.
Given P(A) = 32/100, P(B) = 14/100, and P(A and B) = 8/100, find P(A or B) in lowest terms.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: In a study, P(passes | attended the workshop) is higher than P(passes) overall. What is the correct interpretation?
choices: The two conditional probabilities are equal, so the order of conditioning never matters.
The two events are mutually exclusive.
The relationship proves that one event causes the other.
Attendance and passing are associated, though this alone does not show that the workshop caused the improvement.

items.prompt: A box holds 7 items, of which 5 are defective. Two are drawn without replacement. Find the probability that both are defective, in lowest terms.
Given P(A and B) = 3/100 and P(B) = 4/100, find P(A | B) as a fraction in lowest terms.
Given P(A) = 32/100, P(B) = 35/100, and P(A and B) = 16/100, find P(A or B) in lowest terms.
